verses.text: [“]You are to build an altar of acacia wood. The altar must be square, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.

xrefs.text: Bezalel constructed the altar of burnt offering from acacia wood. It was square, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.

You are to make for Me an altar of earth, and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and peace offerings, your sheep and goats and cattle. In every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
And Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. Early the next morning he got up and built an altar at the base of the mountain, along with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils; consecrate the altar, and it shall be most holy.
And that day Gad came to David and said to him, “Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”

verses.text: Make a horn on each of its four corners, so that the horns are of one piece, and overlay it with bronze.

xrefs.text: The LORD is God; He has made His light to shine upon us. Bind the festal sacrifice with cords to the horns of the altar.

The priest must then put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that is before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting. And he is to pour out the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
But Adonijah, in fear of Solomon, got up and went to take hold of the horns of the altar.
Take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger; then pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
Thus by two unchangeable things in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be strongly encouraged.

verses.text: Make all its utensils of bronze— its pots for removing ashes, its shovels, its sprinkling bowls, its meat forks, and its firepans.

xrefs.text: and the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. All the articles that Huram made for King Solomon in the house of the LORD were made of burnished bronze.
the weight of the pure gold for the forks, sprinkling bowls, and pitchers; the weight of each gold dish; the weight of each silver bowl;
Additionally, Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished all the work that he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of the LORD:
and the pots, shovels, meat forks, and all the other articles. All these objects that Huram-abi made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD were of polished bronze.
He made all the altar’s utensils of bronze— its pots, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks, and firepans.

verses.text: Construct for it a grate of bronze mesh, and make a bronze ring at each of the four corners of the mesh.

xrefs.text: He made a grate of bronze mesh for the altar under its ledge, halfway up from the bottom.
the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grate, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;
Cast four gold rings for it and fasten them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two on the other.

verses.text: Set the grate beneath the ledge of the altar, so that the mesh comes halfway up the altar.

xrefs.text: He made a grate of bronze mesh for the altar under its ledge, halfway up from the bottom.

verses.text: Additionally, make poles of acacia wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze.

xrefs.text: The men registered by their clans numbered 3,200.
the table with its poles, all its utensils, and the Bread of the Presence;
And make two gold rings below the molding on opposite sides to hold the poles used to carry it.

verses.text: The poles are to be inserted into the rings so that the poles are on two sides of the altar when it is carried.

xrefs.text: And make two gold rings below the molding on opposite sides to hold the poles used to carry it.
Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, so that the table may be carried with them.
Then they shall remove the ashes from the bronze altar, spread a purple cloth over it,

verses.text: Construct the altar with boards so that it is hollow. It is to be made just as you were shown on the mountain.

xrefs.text: See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.
You must make the tabernacle and design all its furnishings according to the pattern I show you.

The place where they serve is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven. This is why Moses was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle: “See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.”
Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the portico of the temple, its buildings, storehouses, upper rooms, inner rooms, and the room for the mercy seat.
If you have died with Christ to the spiritual forces of the world, why, as though you still belonged to the world, do you submit to its regulations:

verses.text: You are also to make a courtyard for the tabernacle. On the south side of the courtyard make curtains of finely spun linen, a hundred cubits long on one side,

xrefs.text: Then he constructed the courtyard. The south side of the courtyard was a hundred cubits long and had curtains of finely spun linen,
Planted in the house of the LORD, they will flourish in the courts of our God.
Outside the inner gate, within the inner court, were two chambers, one beside the north gate and facing south, and another beside the south gate and facing north.
Gallery faced gallery in three levels opposite the twenty cubits that belonged to the inner court and opposite the pavement that belonged to the outer court.
Solomon built the inner courtyard with three rows of dressed stone and one row of trimmed cedar beams.

verses.text: with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.

xrefs.text: Each pillar was eighteen cubits tall and twelve cubits in circumference; each was hollow, four fingers thick.
with forty silver bases under the twenty frames— two bases for each frame, one under each tenon.
together with five posts and their hooks. He overlaid the tops of the posts and their bands with gold, and their five bases were bronze.

verses.text: Likewise there are to be curtains on the north side, a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The curtains on the west side of the courtyard shall be fifty cubits wide, with ten posts and ten bases.
The east side of the courtyard, toward the sunrise, is to be fifty cubits wide.
Make the curtains on one side fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases,

xrefs.text: For the entrance to the tent, you are to make a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen.
You are also to make a courtyard for the tabernacle. On the south side of the courtyard make curtains of finely spun linen, a hundred cubits long on one side,

verses.text: and the curtains on the other side fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
The gate of the courtyard shall be twenty cubits long, with a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. It shall have four posts and four bases.

xrefs.text: For the entrance to the tent, you are to make a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen.
In colorful garments she is led to the king; her virgin companions are brought before you.
You are to weave the tunic with fine linen, make the turban of fine linen, and fashion an embroidered sash.
Make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it.
and the sash of finely spun linen, embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

verses.text: All the posts around the courtyard shall have silver bands, silver hooks, and bronze bases.
The entire courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with curtains of finely spun linen five cubits high, and with bronze bases.
All the utensils of the tabernacle for every use, including all its tent pegs and the tent pegs of the courtyard, shall be made of bronze.

xrefs.text: The words of the wise are like goads, and the anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd.
the bases for the surrounding courtyard and its gate, and all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and its surrounding courtyard.

But now, for a brief moment, grace has come from the LORD our God to preserve for us a remnant and to give us a stake in His holy place. Even in our bondage, our God has given us new life and light to our eyes.

the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases; the curtain for the gate of the courtyard, its ropes and tent pegs, and all the equipment for the service of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting;
the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard, along with their ropes;

verses.text: And you are to command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to keep the lamps burning continually.

xrefs.text: Then the LORD said to Moses,
You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
Then I asked the angel, “What are the two olive trees on the right and left of the lampstand?”
the pure gold lampstand with its row of lamps and all its utensils, as well as the oil for the light;
But the olive tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my oil that honors both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’

verses.text: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil that is in front of the Testimony, Aaron and his sons are to tend the lamps before the LORD from evening until morning. This is to be a permanent statute for the Israelites for the generations to come.

xrefs.text: This is a permanent statute for the people: The one who sprinkles the water of purification must wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification will be unclean until evening.

The Levites are to perform the work of the Tent of Meeting, and they must bear their iniquity. This is a permanent statute for the generations to come. The Levites will not receive an inheritance among the Israelites.

Every morning and every evening they present burnt offerings and fragrant incense to the LORD. They set out the rows of showbread on the ceremonially clean table, and every evening they light the lamps of the gold lampstand. We are carrying out the requirements of the LORD our God, while you have forsaken Him.
When Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he must burn the incense perpetually before the LORD for the generations to come.
This is a permanent statute for the generations to come, wherever you live: You must not eat any fat or any blood.”
